rows.title: Generating accurate OpenAPI descriptions from Java source code
rows.authors: Alexander Lercher; David Jamnig; Christian Macho; Clemens Bauer
rows.abstract: Developers require accurate descriptions of REpresentational State Transfer (REST) Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) for implementing successful interactions between web services. The OpenAPI Specification (OAS) has become the de facto standard for documenting REST APIs. Manually creating an OpenAPI description is time-consuming and error-prone, and therefore, several approaches were proposed to automatically generate them from source code or runtime information. rows.title: Fault Injection in OpenAPI Specifications for Evaluating Black-Box Testing Effectiveness
rows.authors: Hamza Bin Mazhar; Yuqing Wang; Mika Mäntylä
rows.abstract: OpenAPI specifications are the primary input for black-box testing tools in microservice systems (MSS), yet prior work shows these specifications are often incomplete, inconsistent, or incorrect. Despite this, most studies on OpenAPI-based black-box testing assume correct specifications and evaluate tool performance. We address this gap by introducing a literature-grounded taxonomy of six OpenAPI specification fault classes. rows.title: Generating REST API Specifications through Static Analysis
rows.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
rows.authors: Ruikai Huang; Manish Motwani; Idel Martinez; Alessandro Orso
rows.abstract: Web Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) allow services to be accessed over the network. RESTful (or REST) APIs, which use the REpresentation State Transfer (REST) protocol, are a popular type of web API. To use or test REST APIs, developers use specifications written in standards such as OpenAPI. rows.abstract: The OpenAPI specification has become a popular tool as it can be used to generate documentation, tests and SDKs. rows.title: SpeCrawler: Generating OpenAPI Specifications from API Documentation Using Large Language Models
rows.authors: Koren Lazar; Matan Vetzler; Guy Uziel; David Boaz
rows.abstract: In the digital era, the widespread use of APIs is evident. However, scalable utilization of APIs poses a challenge due to structure divergence observed in online API documentation. This underscores the need for automatic tools to facilitate API consumption. A viable approach involves the conversion of documentation into an API Specification format. While previous attempts have been made using rule-based methods, these approaches encountered difficulties in generalizing across diverse documentation. rows.title: Implementation of OpenAPI Wireshark Dissectors to Validate SBI Messages of 5G Core Networks
rows.authors: Lukas Schauer; Thorsten Horstmann; Steffen Drusedow; Michael Rademacher
rows.abstract: This paper introduces a novel Wireshark dissector designed to facilitate the analysis of Service-Based Interface (SBI) communication in 5G Core Networks. Our approach involves parsing the OpenAPI schemes provided by the 5G specification to automatically generate the dissector code. Our tool enables the validation of 5G Core Network traces to ensure compliance with the specifications.
